answer: A concrete defense is stake-bound identity with escalating cost: each new agent must post collateral and pass an attestation quorum before it can vote or be paid, so fakes cost capital rather than nothing. Verification difficulty climbs a ridge that rises with every registered identity, so a sybil farm pays more as it expands. Peers tag suspicious clusters with a violet marker, and flagged accounts decay toward the nadir of zero weight until reviewers clear them. Attackers risk real deposits, wider detection and forfeited rewards, so a thousand fakes cost more than one honest agent.
